To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a dynamic programming algorithm is an appropriate tool for gene assembly; (ii) the GRAIL system can accurately recognize coding regions and predict exon candidates; and (iii) GAP III can efficiently construct gene models from accurately-predicted exon candidates, and the models are highly accurate.

(i) a dynamic programming algorithm, GAP III, has been developed for the construction of gene models; (ii) the algorithm constructs gene models with a high degree of accuracy; (iii) it is computationally efficient; and (iv) it can be applied to the construction of gene model for the entire human genome.
GAP III constructs gene models from a given set of accurately predicted exons, and that GAP III performs very well on a test set of human and mouse genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational methods for the automatic construction of gene models from accurately-predicted exons.
the development of a system for constructing gene models.
the construction of gene models from a large set of accurately predicted exon candidates, which are the output of a new version of GRAIL coding region prediction system, GRAIL II.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GAP III is a fast and accurate algorithm for gene model construction.
GAP III can construct gene models from a list of exon candidates with an accuracy of 90%, and that the running time is linearly proportional to (E X C).
GAP III can construct a high quality gene model, complete and/or partial, from a set of exon candidates generated by GRAIL III, and that it is computationally efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GAP III algorithm is a useful tool for constructing gene models and it can serve as a component in a complete gene-finding system.
the GRAIL coding regions recognition system can accurately recognize exons, and GAP III can construct gene models from these accurately-predicted exons.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, given a good set of exon candidates, the construction of gene models is not difficult and can be done efficiently.
, if we have an accurate prediction of the exons in a DNA sequence, we can use GAP III to construct the gene model of this sequence with a very high degree of accuracy.
, given a set of exon candidates with high probability of being true exons, a dynamic programming algorithm can construct gene models that match the structures of actual genes very closely.
